newsitem.title: USA: Martin Luther King family says assassin deserves trial.
newsitem.headline: Martin Luther King family says assassin deserves trial.

text.p: Martin Luther King's family called on Thursday for a trial for the late civil rights leader's confessed assassin, James Earl Ray, charging that the public had not been told the full truth about the assassination.
King's widow and four children threw their support behind Ray's request for a trial in Memphis, Tennessee, where the civil rights leader was gunned down on April 4, 1968, by a sniper's bullet.

King's youngest son, Dexter King, told a news conference he believed that a trial would "probably" vindicate Ray and cast suspicion on a number of shadowy figures. He said he also intended to meet Ray.

He revealed that his father's former associates in Memphis claim to have identified someone other than Ray as the real gunman. He also speculated that renegade federal agents could have been involved in a conspiracy, particulary given his father's growing opposition to the Vietnam War.

"For the sake of truth and justice, we ask that a trial for James Earl Ray be expeditiously set and conducted," Dexter King declared, standing at a podium with his mother, Coretta Scott King, his brother and two sisters.

"The lack of a satisfactory resolution to questions surrounding the assassination of Martin Luther King Jr. has been a source of continuing pain and hardship to our family. Every effort must be made to determine the truth ... this can only be accomplished in a court of law."

The family chose to speak out now because of the declining health of the 68-year-old Ray, who suffers from cirrhosis of the liver. The Kings also received a plea for assistance from Ray's relatives late in January.
"Timing is of the essence, needless to say, because if Mr. Ray does not pull through then, certainly, this will die with him," said Dexter King.
King planned to meet with Ray and hear his story in person, saying he hoped to forgive the former petty crook for whatever role he actually played in the assassination.

Ray was sentenced to 99 years in prison after he confessed to shooting Martin Luther King on the balcony of the Lorraine Motel in Memphis. The confession protected him from a possible death penalty. But he soon recanted the statement and asked for a trial, which was never granted.
Ray's latest request was scheduled to be heard in Shelby County criminal court in Memphis on Feb. 20. Dexter said that he and other King family members planned to attend.

"The public has not been totally given the full truth," said King. "It's time to come clean, and it's time to start letting people know that in order for this nation to come together, we have to deal with the sins of our past."

Relatives and former associates of the civil rights leader have never believed Ray's confession told the full story. Dexter King said his family was dissatisifed with investigations into the muder, including a probe by the U.S. House of Representatives.
Noting Ray's 8th grade education and lack of financial resources, he said the family doubted such a man could elude the FBI and travel abroad without money and assistance from others.

"It's no secret that my father during that time was considered enemy No. 1 to the establishment. It's no secret that he was not the most favourite person of J. Edgar Hoover, the head of the FBI," said Dexter King.

"There may have been individuals (in the government) who saw him as a major threat. The country was in turmoil at the time, I guess you could say civil unrest, and this frightened many people. So, certainly there would be adequate motive."
